title: BatchCache Recommender + Safe Apply Auto-Restore
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Operators routinely tune batching and KV-prefix caching to reduce per-token cost. Changes to default batching, cache TTL, or cache partitioning can improve cost but occasionally cause latency spikes, cold-cache regressions, or correctness regressions when the prefix cache interacts poorly with multi-tenant workloads. We need a single automated flow that: (1) generates recommended batch/cache config deltas based on workload telemetry and cost models, (2) applies those config changes safely (preflight, canary, snapshot), and (3) automatically and reversibly restores prior state if safety signals trigger. This ticket implements the orchestration glue and safety triggers for the auto-restore flow.

Scope and goals:
- Implement a "BatchCache Recommender" service that suggests concrete config patches (batching target, min/max batch size, prefix cache TTL, per-route cache partitions) with expected cost delta and latency impact estimates.
- Implement a safe-apply pipeline: snapshot current config, dry-run simulation (local simulator + policy checks), gradual canary rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%), and automatic rollback conditions.
- Implement an auto-restore controller that reconciles applied vs observed state and performs a deterministic rollback with post-mortem telemetry when guardrails are violated.

Non-goals: full ML-driven model changes, user-facing recommendations UI (we'll expose a simple approve modal in Console but not complex UX in this ticket).

Design highlights (high level):
- Recommendation engine inputs: 7-day request distribution, token mix, observed KV-cache hit rates, current batching latency histogram, cost-per-token baselines, and recent eval set scores for quality-sensitive routes. It outputs a prioritized list of config deltas with an expected cost savings and predicted 95th-p99 latency impact band.
- Preflight simulator: run a short synthetic replay (in a dedicated sandbox cluster) using historical traces to estimate cold-start and cache-warmup behavior. Fail fast if predicted p95 latency increases >10% or quality score drop >3%.
- Snapshotting: before any apply, persist a compact config snapshot plus a serialized cluster-state fingerprint (running version, active kernels, KV-cache map) to S3 with a monotonically-increasing apply_id.
- Canary strategy: route selection by customer/route tag. Canary windows: 10% for 15m, 50% for 30m. Progressive rollback if any threshold breached.
- Guardrails/auto-restore triggers: see acceptance criteria below.

Operational notes:
- All applies go through the controller which writes events to event-log and triggers telemetry annotations so Console can show the live apply_id and decision.
- Expose a manual "force-commit" and "force-rollback" for SREs with audit logging.
- The auto-restore must be idempotent and safe if partially applied (we use two-phase apply with a commit marker).
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation engine produces config deltas with expected cost delta and confidence score for 80% of monitored routes.
Preflight simulation prevents applies where predicted p95 latency regression > 10% or eval quality regression > 3%.
Every apply produces a snapshot with apply_id and persists to S3; apply can be rolled back to that snapshot automatically.
Auto-restore triggers and executes rollback within the canary window when any guardrail is violated (see telemetry thresholds).
Rollback operation must restore KV-cache-safe state (prefix quarantine) and resume normal traffic without manual intervention 95% of the time in integration tests.
Console shows an apply timeline with annotated metrics and a link to the snapshot and PR that generated the change.
telemetry_metrics: KV-cache hit rate by prefix and route
error rate and model quality regression (eval harness)
rollback count, time-to-rollback, and percent of automated rollbacks vs manual
guardrail_thresholds: Immediate rollback if p95 latency increases >= 15% relative to baseline for any canary route sustained for > 5 minutes
Abort (no commit) if preflight sim predicts p95 latency increase >= 10% or quality regression >= 3%
Graceful rollback if cost per token increases > 20% without corresponding quality gains after a full ramp
Rollback if KV-cache hit-rate drops by > 25% for the route's primary prefixes and errors increase by > 0.5%
Manual override allowed by SRE with documented reason and audit log entry
implementation_plan: Week 1: Instrument telemetry collectors and assemble 7-day aggregation job (ENG infra + Observability) - PR # TBD
Week 2: Implement lightweight BatchCache Recommender (heuristic rules + linear cost model) and expose an API endpoint for suggestions
Week 3: Build preflight simulator harness (sandbox replay) and integrate with recommender pipeline
Week 4: Implement apply controller with snapshotting, two-phase commit marker, and canary routing hooks
Week 5: Implement auto-restore controller, guardrail listeners, and Console annotations; run integration + chaos tests
Week 6: Run staged rollout on internal/staging tenants, monitor, and iterate on thresholds
rollout_plan: Start on staging clusters with internal tenants only. Run 100 simulated applies using synthetically generated traces including worst-case cold-cache scenarios. If results stable, enable for 'low-risk' customers (non-financial routes) with auto-restore enabled. After 2 weeks of stable results, expand to opt-in customer beta. Provide SRE playbook for forced rollback and post-mortem steps.
test_plan: Unit tests for recommender cost model and threshold evaluation
Integration test: end-to-end staging apply with snapshot and automated rollback assertion
Chaos test: simulate SLI spike in canary routes and verify rollback triggers within 3 minutes
Replay test: run preflight simulator against 72-hour trace and validate prediction error < 12% for p95 latency
